content: The following antimicrobial agents are categorized based on their association with the risk of Torsades de Pointes (TdP), a potentially life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia: Drugs with a Known Risk of TdP 1. Azithromycin (Zithromax®, Zmax®): A macrolide antibiotic associated with a well-documented risk of TdP. 2. Chloroquine (Aralen®): An antimalarial agent with a known potential to prolong the QT interval and induce TdP. 3. Ciprofloxacin (Cipro®, Cipro-XR®, Neofloxin®): A fluoroquinolone antibiotic linked to QT prolongation and TdP. 4. Clarithromycin (Biaxin®, Prevpac®): Another macrolide antibiotic with a significant risk of TdP. 5. Erythromycin (A/T/S®, Akne-Mycin®, Emgel®, Ery-Tab®, Eryc®, Erycette®, Eryderm®, Erygel®): A macrolide with a well-established association with TdP. 6. Fluconazole (Diflucan®, Trican®): An antifungal agent that can prolong the QT interval and lead to TdP. 7. Halofantrine (Halfan®): An antimalarial drug with a high risk of QT prolongation and TdP. 8. Levofloxacin (Levaquin®, Tavanic®): A fluoroquinolone antibiotic associated with TdP. 9. Moxifloxacin (Avelox®, Avalox®, Avelon®): Another fluoroquinolone with a known risk of TdP. 10. Pentamidine (Pentam®): An antimicrobial agent with a significant risk of QT prolongation and TdP. 11. Sparfloxacin (Zagam®): A fluoroquinolone antibiotic linked to TdP. Drugs with a Possible Risk of TdP 1. Atazanavir (Reyataz®): An antiretroviral agent with a potential risk of TdP. 2. Bedaquiline (Sirturo®): A drug used for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, associated with QT prolongation. 3. Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine (Eurartesim®): An antimalarial combination with a possible risk of TdP. 4. Foscarnet (Foscavir®): An antiviral agent with a potential to prolong the QT interval. 5. Gatifloxacin (Tequin®): A fluoroquinolone antibiotic with a possible risk of TdP. 6. Gemifloxacin (Factive®): Another fluoroquinolone with a potential association with TdP. 7. Norfloxacin (Noroxin®, Ambigram®): A fluoroquinolone antibiotic with a possible risk of TdP. 8. Ofloxacin (Floxin®): A fluoroquinolone with a potential risk of TdP. 9. Rilpivirine (Edurant®, Complera®, Eviplera®): An antiretroviral agent with a possible risk of TdP. 10. Roxithromycin (Rulide®, Xthrocin®, Roxl-150®, Roxo®, Surlid®, Rulide®, Biaxsig®, Roxar®, Roximycinv®, Roxomycin®, Rulid®, Tirabicin®, Coroxin®): A macrolide antibiotic with a potential risk of TdP. 11. Saquinavir (Invirase®): An antiretroviral agent with a possible risk of TdP. 12. Telavancin (Vibativ®): A lipoglycopeptide antibiotic with a potential risk of TdP. 13. Telithromycin (Ketek®): A ketolide antibiotic with a possible risk of TdP. Drugs with Conditional Risk of TdP 1. Amantadine (Symmetrel®, Symadine®): An antiviral and antiparkinsonian agent with a conditional risk of TdP. 2. Hydroxychloroquine (Plaquenil®, Quineprox®): An antimalarial and immunomodulatory drug with a conditional risk of TdP. 3. Itraconazole (Sporanox®, Onmel®): An antifungal agent with a conditional risk of TdP. 4. Ketoconazole (Nizoral®, Sebizole®, Ketomed®, Keton®): Another antifungal with a conditional risk of TdP. 5. Metronidazole (Flagyl® and others): An antimicrobial agent with a conditional risk of TdP. 6. Nelfinavir (Viracept®): An antiretroviral agent with a conditional risk of TdP. 7. Posaconazole (Noxafil®, Posamol®): An antifungal agent with a conditional risk of TdP. 8. Quinine sulfate (Qualaquin®): An antimalarial drug with a conditional risk of TdP. 9. Ritonavir (Norvir®): An antiretroviral agent with a conditional risk of TdP. 10. Telaprevir (Incivek®, Incivo®): An antiviral agent with a conditional risk of TdP. 11. Voriconazole (VFend®): An antifungal agent with a conditional risk of TdP. Drugs to Be Avoided in Patients with Congenital Long QT Syndrome 1. Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (Septra®, Bactrim®, Sulfatrim®, Biseptol®, Co-trimoxazole®, Cotrim®, Septrin®, Trisul®): A combination antibiotic that should be avoided in patients with congenital Long QT syndrome due to its TdP risk. TdP Risk Stratification Schedules for Antimicrobial Agents Schedule I: Drugs with the highest risk of TdP (>1%) and potent IKr blockade. No specific drugs listed. Schedule II: Drugs with significant TdP risk, particularly when coadministered with CYP inhibitors. No specific drugs listed. Schedule III: Drugs with a described risk of TdP and IKr blockade, especially when coadministered with CYP inhibitors: Clarithromycin (Biaxin®, Prevpac®) Erythromycin (A/T/S®, Akne-Mycin®, Emgel®, Ery-Tab®, Eryc®, Erycette®, Eryderm®, Erygel®) Itraconazole (Sporanox®, Onmel®) Ketoconazole (Nizoral®, Sebizole®, Ketomed®, Keton®) Pentamidine (Pentam®) Sparfloxacin (Zagam®) Schedule IV: Drugs with minimal TdP risk, case reports of TdP, mild IKr blockade, and possible CYP interactions: Fluconazole (Diflucan®, Trican®) Gatifloxacin (Tequin®) Gemifloxacin (Factive®) Levofloxacin (Levaquin®, Tavanic®) Moxifloxacin (Avelox®, Avalox®, Avelon®) Telithromycin (Ketek®) Voriconazole (VFend®) Schedule V: Drugs with questionable or minimal risk for QT interval prolongation or TdP: Azithromycin (Zithromax®, Zmax®) Ciprofloxacin (Cipro®, Cipro-XR®, Neofloxin®) Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (Septra®, Bactrim®, Sulfatrim®, Biseptol®, Co-trimoxazole®, Cotrim®, Septrin®, Trisul®)
